verdict.summary: Sterling is a profitable infrastructure contractor with unusually strong data-center and manufacturing exposure, but the current growth rate includes large acquisitions. Q2 revenue rose 90% to $1.17 billion; CEC and Stone Ridge contributed $250.8 million, while management said organic growth was approximately 50%. GAAP net income increased 120% to $155.8 million, adjusted EPS rose 116% to $5.80 and adjusted EBITDA margin reached about 22%. Backlog was $4.33 billion, up 116%, but combined backlog of $5.62 billion includes $1.28 billion of unsigned awards, mostly from acquired businesses. E-Infrastructure is the engine: mission-critical data centers, manufacturing and semiconductor work represented 92% of its backlog. Transportation and Building were weaker. Management raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $19.70-$20.30. The A- grade remains justified, but trade status stays wait because no regular-session opening bar was captured; the $512.36 activation and August 25 structural stop at $480.5799 remain inactive.

Stone Ridge and CEC integration, project concentration and fixed-price cost overruns can reverse margin expansion.

business.overview:
Sterling operates through E-Infrastructure, Transportation and Building Solutions. E-Infrastructure performs site development and electrical work for data centers, manufacturing and semiconductor facilities; Transportation builds public roads and related assets; Building supplies concrete and plumbing work to housing and commercial projects.

The AI transmission channel is physical: hyperscaler and enterprise compute spending becomes data-center land preparation, utilities and mission-critical electrical work. CEC expanded Sterling from site development into electrical services, increasing the amount of each project the company can capture. At Q2, mission-critical work represented 92% of E-Infrastructure backlog and carried the growth profile.

The model breaks if data-center awards are delayed, acquired businesses miss margin targets, unsigned awards fail to convert, or fixed-price labor and material costs outrun estimates. Housing affordability is already pressuring Building, while Sterling is deliberately shifting resources away from lower-growth Transportation projects toward higher-margin E-Infrastructure assignments.
business.moat: Sterling's moat is execution capacity in complex site-development and electrical packages, regional operating density, customer relationships and a safety/selection discipline that favors higher-margin work. CEC broadens the service stack, but the moat depends on maintaining project-level margins while integrating acquisitions and scaling labor.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026 GAAP revenue rose 90% to $1.17B, including $250.8M from acquisitions. GAAP net income was $155.8M and diluted EPS was $5.00, both up more than 115%; non-GAAP adjusted EPS rose 116% to $5.80 and adjusted EBITDA reached $256.7M, a 22% margin. Signed backlog was $4.33B and combined backlog was $5.62B, but the latter includes $1.28B of unsigned awards. Management raised GAAP EPS guidance to $17.25-$17.85 and adjusted EPS guidance to $19.70-$20.30. The caveat is acquisition contribution and uneven segments: Transportation revenue fell 20% and Building fell 1%. The official IR calendar and filings reviewed through August 28 do not announce the next earnings date, so it remains not confirmed.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Sterling ended Q2 with $464.5M of cash against $336.8M of reported debt and generated $328.0M of operating cash flow in the first half. The May S-3ASR provides broad registration capacity, but the reviewed filing row does not establish that Sterling sold stock through an ATM; shelf boilerplate must not be treated as issuance. Approximate diluted shares in 2026 guidance are 31.1M versus 30.9M in 2025. Capital-structure risk is therefore acquisition leverage, earn-outs and integration rather than observed serial equity issuance.

filingsReview.summary: 4 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade A- measures fundamentals; trade state wait measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The June 2026 Form 10-Q supports Sterling's $464.5 million cash balance, $336.8 million debt, project-accounting policies, backlog obligations and acquisition-related assets and liabilities used in the quality review.

The 2025 Form 10-K establishes Sterling's three-segment baseline, historical margins, project and customer concentration, acquisition strategy, internal controls and fixed-price execution risks before the 2026 acquisitions.
The August 3 Form 8-K furnished Q2 results showing $1.17 billion revenue, $5.00 GAAP EPS, $5.80 adjusted EPS and raised 2026 adjusted-EPS guidance of $19.70 to $20.30.

The May 12 automatic shelf provides broad registration capacity for future securities, but no transaction-specific supplement or displayed filing evidence establishes an ATM sale, share issuance or proceeds received.

The S-3ASR is registration capacity, not evidence of ATM issuance.

macro.impact: STRL is a second-order beneficiary of AI and electrification capex: data-center and semiconductor spending becomes site development and electrical backlog. It is also exposed to public infrastructure budgets, labor and materials inflation, and housing affordability. The strongest blast-radius link is mission-critical E-Infrastructure, not the weaker Building segment.

Do not chase a contract award or a move through $512.36 while the earnings date is unconfirmed.
